traps: Workers verify only --lib and named suites; a behaviour change needs the whole-workspace nextest run with --no-fail-fast (c92f4011 r1).
Never wrap land.sh in `jit worktree exec`: it takes the repository lock itself, so nesting waits on its own parent.
Plan and manifest edits in main's checkout block other leads' land.sh; edit in scratch, then copy and commit in one command.
User principle: each code, criterion or wording change is justified on its own merit, never to pre-empt a review.
Unquoted heredocs (<<EOF) in brief generation command-substitute backticked names; use <<'EOF' for any text holding backticks (6ba4f623 brief).

dispatch-worker-worktree.sh refuses whenever main's checkout has any tracked change, including other leads' tracker files: commit a tracker sync immediately before dispatching, and check the [ok] line before writing briefs (03c59566, wave 7).

Pipelines wait at most 30 min for load<4, then run CI (user ruling); exit 75 suite-budget faults are known environment faults until 88's f487aeef. Never launch a pipeline with & inside a foreground Bash call; use run_in_background.

A nextest TIMEOUT on a normally millisecond test is a host artifact (cargo-pool-run waits for a jobserver token inside nextest's timer): rerun, never rework. Host measures: TMPDIR=/mnt/nvme/jit/tmp/9876-lead, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; reclaim worktrees as issues land; never touch the cache pool.

Codex workers never merge main or run any git write (read-only metadata leaves half-merges or copies main's uncommitted .jit lines); the lead merges main into Codex branches and commits their diffs with git add -A crates.

A cargo-ci gate run that fails instantly with exit_code null and empty output was REUSED from a prior failed run with the same inputs digest (origin.derivation=reused). After an environment-faulted failure, re-evaluate with `jit gate evaluate <id> cargo-ci --force`.
Do not set TMPDIR to /mnt/nvme for tests: ext4 directory order breaks a drift test (3e's bug, fix with 944edb32) and fsync-heavy tests time out. ENOSPC under /tmp is a host fault: rerun.

/tmp ENOSPC was inode exhaustion (1.0M inodes; ~473K in leaked /tmp/.tmp* test dirs). Authoritative runs (branch CI, cargo-ci gates) use TMPDIR=/dev/shm/jit-ci/9876a23a under the full-CI lock, created before and removed after each run; workers use /mnt/nvme/jit/tmp/9876-workers (steward rule).
Edits to land-pipeline.zsh only while no pipeline runs it: zsh reads the script while it executes.
Wave ordering that reuses another task's code must be a dependency edge, not sub-wave order (steward, 2026-11-04).

No advisory test suite of this lead (worker or integrator) runs while an authoritative CI run holds the full-CI lock (steward rule, 2026-11-04). Advisory: `flock -o /tmp/jit-ci-turnstile.lock flock -o -s /tmp/jit-full-ci.lock cargo nextest ...`; authoritative: the same turnstile then `-x` (land-pipeline.zsh). The turnstile prevents shared-lock starvation. Overlap pushed 1f24e3e9 cargo-ci to 42 s against the 30 s budget.
Format 4 stores gate runs at .jit/gate-runs/<issue-uuid>/<run-uuid>.json (land-pipeline ENOSPC check updated).

Never land a docs change without branch CI: generated references (docs/reference/gate-presets.md and others) have conformance tests; 62f836117 hand-edited one and turned main red for every lead. Edit the source render and regenerate.
